Zakroczym Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakroczym, Poland

Demolished. Jews are recorded in Zakroczym from the 15th century, though the community only developed significantly after Poland's third partition; by 1893, Jews made up over 60% of the town's population (3,046 residents), falling to 38% by 1921. The cemetery was likely established around 1820, alongside the formation of an independent Jewish community. In September 1939, the Polish Army established a defensive position on the grounds, damaging the site; locals later stole matzevot for construction and grinding wheels. Part of the plot now serves as a strawberry plantation. Germans deported the town's Jews to Pomiechówek and the Nowy Dwór Mazowiecki Ghetto; most died in the following years, including at Auschwitz-Birkenau.
